Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:10:1.english: [It is] pure — apparently it requires intention - [This is stated] in a calm tone [i.e., as an affirmative statement, not as a question].

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:10:2.hebrew: דבש בכוורתו - ואכתי לא חשיב עליה, שהרי הוא בכוורתו. ובדבש דבורים מיירי, דאין כוורת אלא לדבורים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:10:2.english: Honey in its hive - And he has not yet had intention regarding it, as it is in its hive. And it is dealing with bee honey, for a hive is only for bees.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:11:1.hebrew: חלי דיחמורתא - כעין ביצי זכר, שהיחמורות מוציאות מרחמן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:11:1.english: The pendant of a female fallow deer - Something like male testicles that female fallow deer discharge from their womb:

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:11:2.hebrew: ואסורין - משום אבר מן החי, שנעקרו מן הזכר ברחם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:11:2.english: And are forbidden - Because of [the prohibition of] a limb from a living animal, as they were torn from the male in the womb.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:11:3.english: Which pursues the hind - To mate with her.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:11:4.english: And they fall out - [The hart] discharges much semen, and it congeals.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:12:1.english: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a donkey - A kind of afterbirth in which the donkey is born.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:13:1.english: Pure - From transmitting ritual impurity through contact and carrying.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:13:2.hebrew: מאי לאו - אפילו הולד והאם מתים, אפ"ה העור אין מטמא. אלמא דאמר: שליא לא מן הולד ולא מן האם, אלא פירשא בעלמא היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:13:2.english: What, is it not - Even [if] the newborn and the mother are dead, even so the skin does not transmit impurity. This proves that which he said: The placenta is neither from the newborn nor from the mother, but rather is merely a secretion.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:14:1.hebrew: ה"ג לא בין הוא חי ואמו חיה בין הוא מת ואמו חיה - שמגוף האם הוא, והרי היא חיה. אבל לגבי אכילה, כי שדית ליה בתר אם — נמי אסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:14:1.english: This is the correct reading: No, whether it is alive and its mother is alive, [or] whether it is dead and its mother is alive - For it is [part] of the body of the mother, and behold, she is alive. But regarding consumption, if you cast it after the mother [i.e., attribute it to her], it is also forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:15:1.english: That swallowed - This implies that they know for certain that it swallowed it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:15:2.hebrew: לפי שאינו גידוליו - אלא כשהוא חי בלעו, אבל גידוליו שרי, שהיוצא מן הטהור טהור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:15:2.english: Because it is not its product - Rather, [the kosher fish] swallowed it while it was alive. But its [own] product is permitted, for that which emerges from a kosher [creature] is kosher.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:16:1.hebrew: אשרוצי אשריץ - דג טהור זה שנמצא בתוך הטמא נשרץ בגופו, ועוברו הוא, ואסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:16:1.english: It spawned [it] - This kosher fish that was found inside the non-kosher [fish] was spawned in its body, and it is its offspring, and is forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:17:1.english: A non-kosher fish bears live young - Its fetus is inside its body, like other domestic animals and wild beasts.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:17:2.english: A kosher fish lays eggs - And it sits upon them and warms them until it brings them out of the shell, like birds.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:17:3.hebrew: אי הכי - דדג טמא משריץ, האי דבלע איעכל והוי ריעי, וזה שנמצא בתוכו אשרוצי אשריציה, ועוברו הוא, וליתסר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:17:3.english: If so - Since a non-kosher fish spawns [offspring], that which it swallowed was digested and became excrement, and this [fish] that was found inside it, it spawned it, and it is its offspring, and let it be forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:18:1.hebrew: דרך בית הריעי - ואי עוברו הוא, בבית הרחם מיבעי ליה לאישתכוחי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:18:1.english: By way of the excretory passage - And if it were its fetus, it should have been found in the womb.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:18:2.hebrew: שמצאו שלם - שנגמרה כל צורתו וגדול הוא. ואי עוברו, לא הוי משתהי ברחם כולי האי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:18:2.english: Where one found it whole - That its entire form was completed and it is large. And if [it were] its offspring, it would not have remained in the womb for so long.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:19:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - מתני' לאו כדחזיניה דבלע, אלא שנמצא בתוכו. והאי דקתני שבלע — כיון דרוב דגים במינן משריצים, וזה השריץ מין אחר, כמו שבלע בפנינו דמי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:19:1.english: Rav Ashi says - The mishna is not [referring to a case] where we saw it swallow [it], but rather where it was found inside it. And that which it taught, "that [it] swallowed" — since the majority of fish spawn [offspring] of their own species, and [for] this [fish to have] spawned another species [would be contrary to the majority], it is considered as if it swallowed [it] in our presence.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:1:1.hebrew: והני נמי - מטמא קאתו, שבתוך הטמא היו, ואע"ג דלאו מגופיה מימצן, אסירי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:1:1.english: And these too - They come from a non-kosher [animal], for they were inside the non-kosher [animal]; and even though they are not extracted from its body, they are forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:20:1.english: Any [animal] that gives birth - That it gives birth to an actual fetus.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:20:2.hebrew: מניק - שיש לו דדים. וכל המטיל ביצים אין לו דדים, ומלקט פירורים ומפרנס בניו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:20:2.english: Nurses - For it has breasts. And anything that lays eggs does not have breasts, and gathers crumbs and feeds its young.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:20:3.hebrew: עטלף - קלב"א שורי"ץ, דומה לעכבר ויש לו כנפים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:20:3.english: A bat - [In Old French:] chalve-soriz [bat]; it is similar to a mouse and has wings.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:4:1.hebrew: שמכניסות אותן לגופן - שאוכלין מפרחי האילן, ומהן נעשה הדבש במעיהן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:4:1.english: Because they bring them into their body - For they eat from the flowers of the tree, and from them the honey is made in their innards.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:4:2.hebrew: ואין ממצים אותו - דובשנו מגופו. וקשיא לרב ששת, דהא הכא, כיון דלאו מגופייהו מימצו, שרי. רב ששת אמר כל שהיה בתוך הטמא, דאמר כר' יעקב: בטעמא דדבש לאו משום שמכניסות אותן לגופן הוא, אלא דרחמנא שרייה בהדיא, וגזירת הכתוב היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:4:2.english: And they do not excrete it - [They do not excrete] its honey from its body. And [this poses a] difficulty for Rav Sheshet, for behold here, since it is not excreted from their body, it is permitted. Rav Sheshet said [that] whatever was inside a non-kosher [animal is forbidden], for he holds in accordance with Rabbi Ya’akov, [who maintains] regarding the reason for honey, that it is not because they bring it into their body, but rather that the Merciful One explicitly permitted it, and it is a scriptural decree.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:7:1.hebrew: שרץ העוף טמא - הוולד ממש, בהדיא כתיב בו (ויקרא י״א:י״ג): ״את אלה תשקצו מן העוף״:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:7:1.english: A non-kosher winged creature - [Regarding] the actual creature itself, it is explicitly written concerning it (Leviticus 11:13): “These you shall detest from among the birds.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:7:2.hebrew: אלא שרץ עוף טמא שאתה אין אוכל - דלהכי דייקא "ואי אתה", דתיהדר ותידוק מיניה: אבל אתה אוכל מה שעוף טמא משריץ, שאינו ולד דוגמתו, כגון דבש. ל"א: אלא שרץ עוף טמא אי אתה אוכל, ומאידך קרא נסיב לה — "מכל שרץ העוף" וגו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:7:2.english: Rather, a non-kosher winged creature that you do not eat - For it was for this reason that it specifically inferred "and you may not [eat]," so that you would turn around and deduce from it: But you may eat that which a non-kosher winged creature discharges, which is not an offspring resembling it, such as honey. Another explanation: "Rather, a non-kosher winged creature you may not eat" — and it derives it from the other verse: "Of all winged swarming creatures..." etc.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:8:1.english: Gizzin and wasps - A species of locust.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:8:2.hebrew: דבש דבורים - דבש סתמא (הוו) קרו ליה. דבש הגזין — הכי הוא דמיקרו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:8:2.english: Honey of bees - People call it simply “honey.” [Whereas] “honey of gizzin” — that is how it is called.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:9:1.hebrew: טהור - מלקבל טומאת אוכלין, דסתמיה לאו לאכילה עד שיחשב עליו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7b:9:1.english: Pure - From contracting the ritual impurity of food, as its default status is not for eating until one designates it [for that].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:12:1.english: "The skin that emerges opposite the face of a donkey" - [Its] explanation is as [stated] above.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:14:1.hebrew: לא בין הוא חי ואמו מתה בין הוא מת ואמו חיה - שהעור בא בין שניהם, מן האם ומן הולד, ולפיכך טהור עד שימותו שניהם. ובקונטרס פירש כך: "בין הוא ואמו חיה, בין הוא מת ואמו חיה" — [אבל] אמו חיה לעולם בעינן. וכמו שפיר' נראה, דמדנקט רב חסדא: "בין הוא מת ואמו מתה", משמע דאין לו סייעתא אלא מהא דמטהרינן בשניהם מתים; אבל אם האחד חי — אין כאן סייעתא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:14:1.english: "No, whether it is alive and its mother is dead, [or] whether it is dead and its mother is alive" - For the skin comes from between both of them, from the mother and from the offspring, and therefore it is pure until both of them die. And in the Kuntres he explained thus: "Whether it [is alive] and its mother is alive, [or] whether it is dead and its mother is alive" — [but] we always require that its mother be alive. And as he explained appears [correct], for since Rav Ḥisda cited: "Whether it is dead and its mother is dead," this implies that he has support only from that which we declare [it] pure when both are dead; but if one [of them] is alive, there is no support here.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:15:1.hebrew: דג טהור שבלע דג טמא אסור באכילה - תימה: במסכת אהלות (פי"א מ"ז) תנו: "כלב שאכל בשר המת, כמה תשהה במעיו? שלשה ימים מעת לעת; ובעופות ובדגים — כדי שתפול לאור ותשרף". אלמא חשיב עכול, והכא נמי לישתרי! ולא מסתבר לחלק בין בשר המת לשאר דברים, דשלשה ימים דכלב משמע בכל דבר; דמדמייתי עלה במסכת שבת פרק השואל (דף קנה:): "יודע הקב"ה בכלב שמזונותיו מועטות, לפיכך משהה אכילתו במעיו שלשה ימים". ויש לחלק בין איסור לטומאה. ויש רוצים להתיר מתוך משנה זו חטה שנמצאת בפסח במעי תרנגולת; ולפי מה שחלקתי בין איסור לטומאה, אין זה ראיה. עוד פירש ר"ת, דשמא יש להחמיר כר' יהודה בן בתירה, דבעי מעת לעת. ואם באנו לומר דאין חילוק בין איסור לטומאה — צ"ל דשמעתא אתיא בלא שהה כדי עיכול. וא"ת: אי לא שהה כדי עיכול, היכי פריך בגמ' "כי חזינא דבלע, נימא: האי איעכל והאי אשרוצי אשריץ"? י"ל: פעם ממהר להתעכל קודם, ולא הוי ככלב דלעולם ג' ימים:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:15:1.english: "A kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish is forbidden to be eaten" - It is puzzling: In Tractate Oholot (11:7), they taught: [With regard to] a dog that ate the flesh of a corpse, how long must it remain in its entrails? Three full days [twenty-four-hour periods]; and in birds and in fish, as long as [it takes for it] to fall into the fire and be burned. Evidently, [after this amount of time] it is considered digested, and here too, let it be permitted! And it is not reasonable to distinguish between the flesh of a corpse and other matters, for the three days of a dog implies regarding everything; as [the Gemara] cites concerning it in Tractate Shabbat, chapter HaSho'el (155b): "The Holy One, Blessed be He, knows of the dog that its sustenance is meager; therefore He causes its food to remain in its entrails for three days." And one can distinguish between [the laws of] forbidden food and [the laws of ritual] impurity. And there are those who wish to permit, based on this mishna, a grain of wheat found on Passover in the entrails of a hen; and according to what I distinguished between forbidden food and impurity, this is no proof. Rabbeinu Tam further explained that perhaps one must be stringent in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, who requires a full twenty-four-hour period [for fish and birds]. And if we come to say that there is no distinction between forbidden food and impurity — one must say that the sugya is dealing with [a case where] it did not remain for the duration of digestion. And if you say: If it did not remain for the duration of digestion, how does the Gemara challenge: "When we saw it swallow, let us say: that [one] was digested, and this [one] it spawned"? One can say: Sometimes it is digested more quickly beforehand, and it is not like a dog, where [it is] always three days.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:19:1.hebrew: רוב דגים במינם משריצים - הלכתא כרב אשי, דהוא בתראה. ויש להתיר אותן דגים שקורין מרנ"ש הנמצא תוך דג בלינ"א, ואע"ג דלא חזינן דבלע. ואין להקשות ממתני' דשריא דג טמא שבלע דג טהור לרב ששת דאסר מי רגלים של חמור — דאפי' ללישנא בתרא דרב ששת, דאסר אף של סוסים וגמל, לא דמי: חדא — דמתני' לא איירי אלא נמצא תוכו דג טהור; ואפילו יצאו, הכא פשיטא דדגים עייל דגים נפיק, אבל מים שהבהמה שותה, לחלוחית הגוף מתערב עמהם. ובת"כ תני גבי דגים: "תאכלו" — לרבות הטהור שבמעי טמא; יכול אף הטמא שבמעי טהור? ת"ל: "אותם". מה ראית לומר בבהמה שבמעי טמא טמא, ושבמעי טהור טהור (מטמא שבמעי הטהור טהור), ובדגים אינו כן? לפי שאין גדוליו. ואין ראיה משם לאסור דג טמא שבלע דג טהור אחר שיצא משום דנקט "שבמעי הטמא" — דלאו דוקא, אלא משום "טמא שבמעי טהור", דדילמא ההיא דשרינן ביצא לחוץ משום דחשיב עיכול:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:19:1.english: The majority of fish spawn their own species - The halakhah follows Rav Ashi, since he is the later [authority]. And [accordingly,] one may permit those fish that they call marensh [herrings] found inside a balena [whale] fish, even though we did not see it swallow [them]. And one should not raise a difficulty from our Mishnah, which permits [eating] a kosher fish that was swallowed by a non-kosher fish, against Rav Sheshet, who prohibited the urine of a donkey; for even according to the latter version of Rav Sheshet's [ruling], who prohibited even [the urine] of horses and camels, it is not comparable: First, our Mishnah only speaks of [a case where] a kosher fish was found inside it; and even if they came out [were excreted], here it is obvious that "fish entered, fish exited," whereas [with] water that the animal drinks, bodily moisture mingles with it. And in Torat Kohanim it is taught regarding fish: "[These] you may eat" (Leviticus 11:9) — to include a kosher [fish] that is in the innards of a non-kosher [fish]. Could [one think that] even a non-kosher [fish] in the innards of a kosher [fish is permitted]? The verse states: "them" [Leviticus 11:9]. What did you see [as the basis] to say regarding an animal that [what is] in the innards of a non-kosher [animal] is non-kosher, and [what is] in the innards of a kosher [animal] is kosher ([or:] from a non-kosher [animal] in the innards of a kosher [animal] is kosher), but regarding fish it is not so? Because it is not its offspring. And there is no proof from there to prohibit a non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish after it came out, [arguing] from the fact that it stated "that is in the innards of the non-kosher [fish]" — for [this formulation] is not exact, but rather [was used] on account of [the parallel clause,] "a non-kosher [fish] in the innards of a kosher [fish]"; for perhaps in that [latter case], it is permitted once it has come outside because it is considered digested [waste].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:20:1.hebrew: דג טמא משריץ דג טהור מטיל ביצים - בע"ז פרק אין מעמידין (עבודה זרה דף מ.) מפרש: תרוייהו מטילי ביצים נינהו — זה משריץ מבחוץ, וזה משריץ מבפנים:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:20:1.english: "A non-kosher fish spawns, a kosher fish lays eggs" - In Avodah Zarah, chapter Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 40a), [the Gemara] explains: Both of them lay eggs — this one [the kosher fish] spawns outside, and that one [the non-kosher fish] spawns inside.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:3:1.hebrew: תניתוה היוצא מן הטמא טמא - הא דמשמע לסימן נקטיה — לא קשה מידי, כדפרישי' לעיל (בכורות דף ו. ד"ה למה):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:3:1.english: "You learned [it in the Mishnah]: That which emerges from the non-kosher is non-kosher" - That which implies that [the Mishnah] stated it [merely] as a mnemonic is not difficult at all, as we explained above (Bekhorot 6a, s.v. Lama).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:8:1.hebrew: הגזין וצרעין - גרסינן, ולא גרסינן חגבים — שזה עוף, כמו גזי דכלתא דנדה (דף יז.), לפי' ר"ת:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7b:8:1.english: "The gizzin and wasps" - We read [this], and we do not read "ḥagavim" [grasshoppers] — for this is a winged creature, like gazei dekhalta [the flies of the canopy] in Niddah (17a), according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam.
